'''Torbjørn Sikkeland''' (3 August 1923 – 7 November 2014) was a Norwegian chemist, nuclear physicist and radiation biophysicist.

He was born in Norway in [[Varteig]]. He was part of the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Berkeley team]] that claimed discovery of the synthetic [[Transuranium element|transuranic elements]] of [[nobelium]] and [[lawrencium]]. He was appointed professor at the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in [[Trondheim]] from 1969 to 1993.<ref name=nbl>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Torbjørn Sikkeland |encyclopedia=[[Norsk biografisk leksikon]]|first=Ivar |last=Svare |authorlink= |editor=Helle, Knut |editor-link=Knut Helle |publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=https://nbl.snl.no/Torbjørn_Sikkeland |language=Norwegian|accessdate=13 September 2014}}</ref><ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Torbjørn Sikkeland |encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor-last=Godal | editor-first=Anne Marit | editor-link=Anne Marit Godal |publisher=Norsk nettleksikon |location=Oslo |url=https://snl.no/Torbjørn_Sikkeland |language=Norwegian |accessdate=13 September 2014}}</ref> He was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntva.no/2013/12/17/sikkeland-torbjorn/|title=SIKKELAND, Torbjørn|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=14 September 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129021413/http://www.ntva.no/2013/12/17/sikkeland-torbjorn/|archivedate=29 November 2014}}</ref>

He died in November 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Torbjørn Sikkeland|last=Henriksen|first=Thormod|date=14 November 2014|work=Aftenposten|page=28|language=Norwegian}}</ref>
